records.purpose: Copy the local player's current item-port snapshot into out (caller sets out->size; out->count is capacity in, ports filled out, max 128). Read-only: per valid port, the attached item's item type id (field item_class_id, an ordinal of the game's item-type enumeration) and its session-scoped entity id (joins game.entities); generation advances on port-set change. Values are the client's view of server state at snapshot time; nothing can be written through this ABI.
records.buffer_contract:
`sco_result (*snapshot)(sco_plugin* self, sc_inventory_snapshot* out);`

Read-only: per valid port, the attached item's item type id (field item_class_id, an ordinal of the game's item-type enumeration) and its session-scoped entity id (joins game.entities); generation advances on port-set change. records.ownership: Provider fills caller-owned storage; a plain copy crosses. No allocation, no engine pointer transfer, nothing retained from out.
records.reentrancy: Snapshot read; no engine re-entry beyond the bound adapter's accessors.
records.results: OK snapshot copied, UNAVAILABLE service off, no backend bound, out null, out->size too small, or no local player; BAD_ARG invalid self.
records.absent_capability: game.inventory.read defaults OFF; unbound production publishes UNAVAILABLE. Enumeration accessors grounded on the private corpus (F-4.10.196.36804-009); no production adapter bound yet.
records.cleanup: StopGameInventory withdraws the service; read-only, no engine state to restore.
limitations: Local player ports only in 1.0 (ships/mounts are follow-ups).
Per-class item names are not yet established; an item-type-id name map exists but is not exposed in 1.0.
Snapshot semantics: 128 ports max; generation detects change; per-frame streams are out of contract.
No C# or Lua game.inventory routes are supported.
